approaches.name: MojTermin COVID-19 screening, monitoring and contact-tracing modules
approaches.description: Adds COVID-19 screening, home-treatment monitoring and contact-tracing modules to the national MojTermin e-health system, linking primary care for real-time reporting. Practices: MojTermin COVID-19 screening and home-treatment monitoring module; MojTermin surveillance and contact-tracing modules linked to primary care.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: pandemic modules in national e-health record - cue: 'new module' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: To facilitate protective measures against COVID-19 by physicians and patients in need of health care, as well as easy recording and analysis of data on patients with COVID-19, the MojTermin team in the Ministry of Health (MoH) has developed a new module, consisting of a COVID-19 screening submodule and submodule for monitoring home-treatment patients with COVID-19.

extra_evidence.text: In addition, data are entered in MojTermin for COVID-19 patients as for patients with any other condition (all checkups, results from diagnostic examinations, medication, etc.), creating a unique resource for monitoring and analyzing data on COVID-19 patients once the system is rolled out countrywide.

It will facilitate combining the detection of new cases with active contact tracing, by enhancing the surveillance and contact tracing modules of the health system’s current information system (MojTermin) and linking primary care providers to it.

Finally, it will help provide on-time and real-time data and information to guide decision-making and response and mitigation activities, by enhancing systems and protocols and building capacity for data reporting, data analysis, and information dissemination.

category.rationale: Technological: the e-health system module is the core mechanism

sector.rationale: MoH e-health record system enhancement is a public health administration function.

approaches.name: Interoperable CBMIS platform for registration, surveys and benefit applications
approaches.description: Uses the interoperable CBMIS beneficiary platform for online and phone registration, repeated phone surveys and a new Employment Agency unemployment benefit application module. Practices: CBMIS-based phone surveys of social assistance beneficiaries; Online and phone registration via interoperable CBMIS platform; New Employment Agency application module for unemployment benefits.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: registry-linked phone survey rounds for impact monitoring - cue: 'phone surveys' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Using the beneficiary information from the Cash Benefits Management Information System (CBMIS), the project will conduct several rounds of phone surveys of social assistance beneficiaries to assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on vulnerable households and on their needs.

extra_evidence.text: Additionally, the project may facilitate citizen engagement activities using the same tool.

Registration and intake for new beneficiaries of the temporary cash assistance will be conducted online, by phone, and in the 30 CSWs and 50 offices located primarily in rural areas (while applying social distancing procedures).
All the necessary documents for benefit application are available electronically through the interoperable CBMIS platform.
The CBMIS IT unit will support the Employment Agency in the process of registration and in the administration of additional unemployment benefits.
This would include information system adaptation and the deployment of a new application module in the Employment Agency.
The system will use the e-platform for online services developed by the Ministry of Information Society and Administration.

category.rationale: Technological: registry data plus phone survey is the core mechanism

sector.rationale: Phone surveys of social assistance beneficiaries directly serve social protection.

approaches.name: online platform for community feedback and grievance redress
approaches.description: Project builds an online platform to collect community feedback and grievances during social distancing
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: online feedback channel replacing in-person community engagement - cue: 'online platform' | category Operational; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: To ensure that communities are engaged while social distancing policies are being implemented, the component will support the development of an online platform for all stages of community feedback.

extra_evidence.text: In addition, the project will implement a feedback mechanism on the COVID-19 response (temporary cash and in-kind benefits and health activities), to ensure communities can provide just-in-time-feedback to government to ensure that investments respond to local needs and reach vulnerable groups.
This will also include a community-based monitoring mechanism and a grievance redress mechanism.

category.rationale: Operational: re-engineers how citizen feedback reaches government

sector.rationale: Community feedback and grievance platform supports social assistance program delivery.
